place_fields.micro_region: Devimane Ghats, near Sirsi, Uttara Kannada, Karnataka
place_fields.summary: Waterfall formed by a tributary of the Aghanashini River, falling about 200 feet in dense Western Ghats forest.

planning_attributes.description: Benne Hole Falls is a waterfall in the Devimane Ghats near Sirsi, formed by a tributary of the Aghanashini River and dropping about 200 feet into a rocky pool.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The Kannada name refers to the waterfall's creamy, butter-like appearance: benne means butter and hole means big stream.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: From Sirsi, travel toward Kumta Road to Kasage, then follow the jeep track toward Hosur; the final approach is about a 2 km walk.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: The final approach involves a forest walk; access becomes difficult during heavy rain and water levels can be high.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Rocky areas can be slippery and swimming at the falls is unsafe, especially when water flow is high; local guidance is advisable.
planning_attributes.notes: There are no food or accommodation facilities immediately at the falls; Sirsi provides nearby services.

place_fields.vibe: quiet forest waterfall and short trek
place_fields.summary: A lesser-known waterfall in the forested Uttara Kannada region near Yellapur.

planning_attributes.description: Kulimagodu Falls is a scenic, relatively uncrowded waterfall in the forest region of Uttara Kannada near Yellapur.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: From Yellapur, the approach includes a road journey followed by a short forest walk or trek.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Rainy-season access can be muddy and more difficult.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Use caution on wet forest paths and around the waterfall during monsoon conditions.
planning_attributes.notes: The falls is described as an offbeat destination with a short approach trek.

place_fields.micro_region: Mattighatta, near Sirsi, Uttara Kannada, Karnataka
place_fields.vibe: remote forest waterfall, trekking and adventure
place_fields.summary: A two-tiered waterfall, also known as Hasehalla Falls, deep in the forest near Sirsi and reached by a demanding trek.

planning_attributes.description: Mattighatta Falls, also known as Hasehalla Falls, is a two-tiered waterfall in dense forest near Sirsi, with a reported drop of about 350 feet.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: Also known as Hasehalla Falls; the waterfall is associated with the Hasehalla stream.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: From Sirsi take the Kumta road to Hegde Katte, then the Mattighatta road via Devanahalli to Mattighatta village; the final approach includes about a 2 km downhill trek and a rocky riverside section.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: The approach is difficult and can become very hard during the rainy season; there are limited facilities and signage.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Expect slippery and rocky terrain, strong water flow and difficult access; caution is particularly important during monsoon conditions.
planning_attributes.notes: A local guide is useful because of the remote approach and limited signage/network coverage in the area.
